<p align="center">
  Claude-Mem seamlessly preserves context across sessions by automatically capturing tool usage observations, generating semantic summaries, and making them available to future sessions. This enables Claude to maintain continuity of knowledge about projects even after sessions end or reconnect.
</p>

---

## Quick Start

Install claude-mem for Grok Bot:

```bash
npx claude-mem install --ide grok-bot
```

Grok Bot has no host hooks, so we watch the chat log files. Default is CMEM Pro, the hosted memory. Local observer is opt-in: `--provider host`. Installing this plugin does not install Cursor.

**Awareness push pilot (LFG + Orifice):** needle observations (`decision`, `bugfix`, `security_alert`, `sensitive`) are appended as dated `- YYYY-MM-DD [awareness] …` lines into that bot's `memory/log/YYYY-MM.md`. Grok Bot already re-reads the log from disk. This does not write `profile.md`, user-memory, or project memory. Disable with `CLAUDE_MEM_GROK_BOT_AWARENESS_ENABLED=false`.

Install with a single command:

```bash
npx claude-mem install
```

The installer sets everything up first, then asks you to sign in to claude-mem in your browser (email magic link — no card required). Signing in provisions a memory key for your account and unlocks the **claude-mem observer** with a **30 Day Free Trial**: memory runs off-plan, so you get up to 100% more usage from your plan. When the free trial ends, memory automatically falls back to your Anthropic plan unless you subscribe. After sign-in you pick your memory provider — the claude-mem observer, your own OpenRouter or Gemini key, or your Anthropic plan.

Prefer to skip the sign-in? Pass an explicit `--provider` flag, set `CLAUDE_MEM_ONLINE_OPTIN=false`, or run in CI/non-interactive shells — the installer completes without any account interaction.

Or install for OpenCode:

```bash
npx claude-mem install --ide opencode
```

This works with OpenCode 1.3.4 or later, including OpenCode 2. Restart OpenCode after installing.

Or install for **T3 Code** (Codex and Claude Code providers):

```bash
npx claude-mem install --ide t3code
```

The installer discovers T3 Code's enabled providers, registers native Claude-Mem plugins in their configured homes, and supports T3-managed Codex. Restart T3 Code, trust the provider's hooks when prompted, and start a new thread. See the [T3 Code integration guide](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/t3code-integration) for custom server settings, status, and removal.

Or install for Antigravity CLI ([setup guide](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/antigravity-cli/setup)):

```bash
npx claude-mem install --ide antigravity
```

Or install for OMP (Oh My Pi):

```bash
npx claude-mem install --ide omp
```

Or install the native Pi extension or DeepSeek Harness plugin:

```bash
npx claude-mem install --ide pi
npx claude-mem install --ide dsh --dsh-profile tui
```

Pi and DeepSeek Harness use the worker runtime. See [native harness setup](docs/native-harness-integrations.md) for capture, recall, and troubleshooting.

Or install from the plugin marketplace inside Claude Code:

```bash
/plugin marketplace add thedotmack/claude-mem

/plugin install claude-mem
```

Restart Claude Code. Context from previous sessions will automatically appear in new sessions.

> **Note:** Claude-Mem is also published on npm, but `npm install -g claude-mem` installs the **SDK/library only** — it does not register the plugin hooks or set up the worker service. Always install via `npx claude-mem install` or the `/plugin` commands above.

### 🦞 OpenClaw Gateway

Install claude-mem as a persistent memory plugin on [OpenClaw](https://openclaw.ai) gateways with a single command:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://install.cmem.ai/openclaw.sh | bash
```

The installer handles dependencies, plugin setup, AI provider configuration, worker startup, and optional real-time observation feeds to Telegram, Discord, Slack, and more. See the [OpenClaw Integration Guide](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/openclaw-integration) for details.

**Key Features:**

- 🧠 **Persistent Memory** - Context survives across sessions
- 📊 **Progressive Disclosure** - Layered memory retrieval with token cost visibility
- 🔍 **Smart Search (Default)** - Query your project history with the three-step mem-search skill
- 🖥️ **Local My Work** - Live requests, progress, human handoffs and a saved review queue at the worker URL printed on startup. [Guide](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/usage/my-work). Memory, sessions and settings remain at `/viewer`.
- 👥 **TeamBrain** - An optional shared workspace beside My Work, with real team work lists, member attribution and linked findings. Each person chooses what to share; personal requests and review notes stay separate. [Set up a team](https://cmem.ai/teambrain/start).
- 💻 **Claude Desktop Skill** - Search memory from Claude Desktop conversations
- 🔒 **Privacy Control** - Use `<private>` tags to exclude sensitive content from storage
- 🖼️ **Screenshots (opt-in, off by default)** - Keep converted copies of tool screenshots under `~/.claude-mem/media-v1/`, upload them to cmem.ai only when Cloud Sync is on, and send them to the observer model only when image inference is separately enabled ([details](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/configuration#screenshots-and-images-opt-in))
- ⚙️ **Context Configuration** - Fine-grained control over what context gets injected
- 🤖 **Automatic Operation** - No manual intervention required
- 🔗 **Citations** - Reference past observations with IDs through the worker API or view all in the web viewer

## How It Works

**Core Components:**

1. **Lifecycle Hooks** - SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop, SessionEnd. Each is one shell-free command, `claude-mem hook claude-code <event>`, run by a small launcher that the installer puts on PATH
2. **Smart Install** - Cached dependency checker (Setup hook on `claude --init` / `--maintenance`, plus `npx claude-mem install` / `repair`)
3. **Worker Service** - Local HTTP API with web viewer UI and search endpoints, managed by Bun
4. **SQLite Database** - Stores sessions, observations, summaries
5. **mem-search Skill** - Natural language queries with progressive disclosure
6. **Chroma Vector Database** - Hybrid semantic + keyword search for intelligent context retrieval

See [Architecture Overview](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/architecture/overview) for details.

---

## MCP Search Tools

Claude-Mem provides intelligent memory search through **4 MCP tools** following a token-efficient **3-layer workflow pattern**:

**The 3-Layer Workflow:**

1. **`search`** - Get compact index with IDs (~50-100 tokens/result)
2. **`timeline`** - Get chronological context around interesting results
3. **`get_observations`** - Fetch full details ONLY for filtered IDs (~500-1,000 tokens/result)

**How It Works:**
- Claude uses MCP tools to search your memory
- Start with `search` to get an index of results
- Use `timeline` to see what was happening around specific observations
- Use `get_observations` to fetch full details for relevant IDs
- **~10x token savings** by filtering before fetching details

**Available MCP Tools:**

1. **`search`** - Search memory index with full-text queries, filters by type/date/project
2. **`timeline`** - Get chronological context around a specific observation or query
3. **`get_observations`** - Fetch full observation details by IDs (always batch multiple IDs)

**Example Usage:**

```typescript
// Step 1: Search for index
search(query="authentication bug", type="bugfix", limit=10)

// Step 2: Review index, identify relevant IDs (e.g., #123, #456)

// Step 3: Fetch full details
get_observations(ids=[123, 456])
```

See [Search Tools Guide](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/usage/search-tools) for detailed examples.

---

## System Requirements

- **Node.js**: 20.0.0 or higher
- **Claude Code**: Latest version with plugin support
- **Bun**: JavaScript runtime and process manager (auto-installed if missing)
- **uv**: Python package manager for vector search (auto-installed if missing)
- **SQLite 3**: For persistent storage (bundled)

---
### Windows Setup Notes

If you see an error like:

```powershell
npm : The term 'npm' is not recognized as the name of a cmdlet
```

Make sure Node.js and npm are installed and added to your PATH. Download the latest Node.js installer from https://nodejs.org and restart your terminal after installation.

Claude Code hooks do not need Git Bash. Each hook runs `claude-mem` directly, and `npx claude-mem install` places that launcher at `%LOCALAPPDATA%\claude-mem\bin\claude-mem.exe` and adds the folder to your user Path. Restart your terminal or IDE afterwards so Claude Code picks up the new Path. If hooks report `Executable not found in $PATH: "claude-mem"`, run `npx claude-mem doctor` and see [Troubleshooting](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/troubleshooting#claude-mem-command-not-found-in-hooks).

---

## Configuration

Settings are managed in `~/.claude-mem/settings.json` (auto-created with defaults on first run). Configure AI model, worker port, data directory, log level, and context injection settings.

To include observations from every harness in Claude Code and Codex SessionStart context, set `"CLAUDE_MEM_SESSION_START_INCLUDE_ALL_SOURCES": "true"` in that file, or enable **Include all sources at session start** in the viewer settings. The default is `"false"`, which limits startup context to the current harness. The observation count limit still applies across the selected sources.

See the **[Configuration Guide](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/configuration)** for all available settings and examples.

### Mode & Language Configuration

Claude-Mem supports multiple workflow modes and languages via the `CLAUDE_MEM_MODE` setting.

This option controls both:
- The workflow behavior (e.g. code, chill, investigation)
- The language used in generated observations

#### How to Configure

Edit your settings file at `~/.claude-mem/settings.json`:

```json
{
  "CLAUDE_MEM_MODE": "code--zh"
}
```

Modes are defined in `plugin/modes/`. To see all available modes locally:

```bash
ls ~/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/thedotmack/plugin/modes/
```

#### Available Modes

| Mode | Description |
|------------|-------------------------|
| `code` | Default English mode |
| `code--zh` | Simplified Chinese mode |
| `code--ja` | Japanese mode |

Language-specific modes follow the pattern `code--[lang]` where `[lang]` is the ISO 639-1 language code (e.g., `zh` for Chinese, `ja` for Japanese, `es` for Spanish).

> Note: `code--zh` (Simplified Chinese) is already built-in — no additional installation or plugin update is required.

#### After Changing Mode

Restart Claude Code to apply the new mode configuration.

# Spotify Portal AI Plugins

Bring [Spotify Portal](https://portal.spotify.com) into Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and pi.

This plugin provides focused workflows for the
[Portal CLI](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@spotify/portal-cli): set up
authentication, search your software catalog, build service briefings, run
diagnostics, and invoke Portal actions.

## Highlights

- Set up the Portal CLI for your current coding-agent environment.
- Run read-only diagnostics to verify plugin, CLI, authentication, and action readiness.
- Search the software catalog and technical documentation using natural language queries.
- Generate concise service briefings with available ownership, health, incident, and documentation details.
- Discover and safely invoke Portal actions with built-in help, dry-run, and confirmation safeguards.
- Create, run, check, and troubleshoot Fleetshift shifts, open PRs from completed runs, and stop a run on request.

The marketplace also ships **shunt** (Claude Code only for now): a plugin that routes I/O-heavy agent work — bulk file reads and boilerplate generation — to AiKA modes running cheaper worker models, via the Portal CLI actions registry. See [`plugins/shunt/README.md`](plugins/shunt/README.md).

## Installation

### Claude Code

```bash
claude plugin marketplace add spotify/portal-ai-plugins
claude plugin install portal@portal
claude plugin install shunt@portal   # optional: token-saving AiKA delegation
```

Start a new session and run:

```text
/portal:setup
```

### Codex

```bash
codex plugin marketplace add spotify/portal-ai-plugins
codex
```

Open `/plugins`, install Spotify Portal, start a new task, and ask:

```text
Set up Spotify Portal for me.
```

### Cursor

Register the [spotify/portal-ai-plugins](https://github.com/spotify/portal-ai-plugins)
repository in your Cursor team marketplace, then install Spotify Portal from
**Cursor Settings → Plugins**.

### pi

```bash
pi install git:github.com/spotify/portal-ai-plugins
```

Start a new session and run:

```text
/skill:setup
```

## Workflows

| Workflow | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `setup` | Configure Portal CLI authentication |
| `doctor` | Run read-only readiness diagnostics |
| `search` | Search the software catalog and technical documentation |
| `service` | Produce a concise operational service briefing |
| `actions` | Discover, inspect, preview, and safely invoke Portal actions |
| `feedback` | Submit feedback about the Portal CLI to the Portal team |
| `fleetshift-create-shift` | Draft and create a Fleetshift shift from a goal, with a dry-run preview |
| `fleetshift-run-shift` | Trigger a shift, monitor it with a bounded wait, and stop it on request |
| `fleetshift-check-shift` | Report a shift's progress, targets, and PRs (read-only) |
| `fleetshift-troubleshoot-shift` | Diagnose failed shift jobs from their status and logs (read-only) |
| `fleetshift-create-prs` | Open PRs for completed shift targets after confirmation |

## Portal CLI

The workflows invoke the upstream CLI through:

```bash
npx @spotify/portal-cli <command>
```

Setup verifies the required `auth`, `actions`, `owner`, `search`, and `service`
commands before proceeding.

## Connect once. Ready whenever you are.

Continue using your DeepSeek Harness instance from a phone, computer, or browser. Return to the same Harness session from whichever device is with you.

Harness keeps running on your work computer, with the same workspaces, tools, and project setup. DS Harness Remote is simply another window into that environment.

The DeepSeek Harness desktop edition is supported. Install the latest release:

`ds-harness-remote@0.6.2`

## Features

- Access your local Harness instance remotely from the web, a PC, or a mobile device: DSH first, with Codex, Cursor, and Antigravity support too.
- DeepSeek Harness Desktop is ready to use after installation, with its native interface and no separate desktop conversation UI.
- Create workspaces, configure models, and switch conversation models with the same smooth workflow as local use.
- No public listening port or public IP is required on the Harness Host. Connect from anywhere with internet access over a bidirectional end-to-end encrypted channel.
- Prefer P2P connections, use TURN relay nodes worldwide, and fall back to multiple Server Relays when needed.
- Access workspace files, read-only previews, remote terminals, and authorized local development-service previews through the native Harness sidebar.
- Remote Tool context injection supports Host and workspace discovery, Harness session creation and management, history reading, waiting for execution, interruption requests, and authorized file transfers. [Details](packages/plugin/README.md#remote-agent-tools).
- Alongside DeepSeek Harness, access native workspaces for Codex, Cursor, Google Antigravity, Pi, OpenCode, Claude Code, Hermes Agent, and other tools through ACP integrations, with remote file browsing and terminals.
- Clients are available across Android, iOS, Web, and native DSH.
- Multiple clients can connect to the same Harness Host simultaneously, with RPC calls and streams isolated per connection.

## Supported clients

| Client | Form | Status | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| DSH Desktop plugin | Remote sidebar | Supported | Install `ds-harness-remote@0.6.2`; this computer can also be the Host |
| Web | Browser page | Supported | Open [https://dsh.r2049.cn](https://dsh.r2049.cn); reuses the native Harness interface |
| Android | Native app | Supported | Download the APK from [Releases](https://github.com/liguobao/ds-harness-remote/releases/latest); see the [Android guide](apps/android/README.md) |
| DSH Go | A standout app by ccch1mneyyy | Supported | See [ccch1mneyyy/dsh-go: an Android client for DeepSeek Harness. Run it directly on your phone or control DSH on your computer remotely.](https://github.com/ccch1mneyyy/dsh-go) |
| iOS | TestFlight beta | Beta | Not publicly released; see [issue #20](https://github.com/liguobao/ds-harness-remote/issues/20) |
| Browser extension | Chrome | Entry point only | Exchanges an already signed-in Web authorization for a separate device credential, lists online Hosts and opens the same-origin Remote Web; it does not host a conversation UI |
| dsh-TUI | Terminal-only CLI | Supported | Can act as a Host; see the [dsh-TUI Remote guide](docs/dsh-tui.md). The installer never creates a Web service for it automatically |
| Linux | Cloud server | Supported | Sign in on the [official website](https://dsh.r2049.cn/) for unattended installation with a single command and no configuration. |

Several clients can connect to the same Host at once; RPC calls and streams are isolated per connection.

## Install

### DeepSeek Harness Desktop support

Open **Extensions / Plugin management** in DeepSeek Harness Desktop, choose installation
from npm, and enter this package:

`ds-harness-remote@0.6.2`

Restart Desktop afterward. Its official `dsh` launcher can also install the pinned package
with `dsh plugin --profile desktop add -w ds-harness-remote@0.6.2`.

### Linux one-command installation

Visit [https://dsh.r2049.cn](https://dsh.r2049.cn/), sign in, and obtain an installation authorization code to install with one command.

### dsh-TUI Host

For terminal Host setup with [dsh-TUI](https://github.com/ccch1mneyyy/dsh-TUI), see the
[dsh-TUI Remote guide](docs/dsh-tui.md).

### Native Android client

Keep conversations connected across multiple workspaces at once, and use **Bot mode**, powered by [Fei2411/DS-Bot](https://github.com/Fei2411/DS-Bot).

Download the latest APK from [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/liguobao/ds-harness-remote/releases/latest), and sign in to the same account to see your Hosts.

## DSH Go — DeepSeek Harness in your pocket: run it locally on your phone or control your computer remotely.

[ccch1mneyyy/dsh-go](https://github.com/ccch1mneyyy/dsh-go) has built-in support for the ds-harness-remote protocol. You can run DeepSeek Harness locally on your phone or connect to your computer remotely.

After installing the ds-harness-remote plugin in DSH Go on your phone, you can also connect to the phone’s DSH from your computer or the web and use Mobile Use seamlessly.

### iOS client

- [Join the beta](https://github.com/liguobao/ds-harness-remote/issues/20)

## Quick start

1. Open **Remote** from the DeepSeek Harness sidebar.
2. Choose Zhihu, GitHub, or Google authorization, or sign in with an account and password. Account registration requires an invitation code; email the repository author to request one.
3. On another device, install the same plugin in DeepSeek Harness and sign in as described in steps 1–2. Alternatively, use Remote Web, iOS, Android, or DSH Go directly without installing a plugin.
4. Select an online Host, then choose an existing workspace or browse remote directories to open one.

By default, Remote uses this project's hosted Server at [https://dsh.r2049.cn](https://dsh.r2049.cn).

For self-hosting, use the repository's [minimal Server](apps/server/README.md). The current version includes P2P coordination and a Relay Server, but does not provide the full hosted Remote Web experience.

## Screenshots

### Desktop

On another computer, select an online Host and open its workspace. The workspace opens in the native Harness interface, with the active Host and encrypted connection status in the header.

<p align="center">
  <img src="docs/images/host-list.png" alt="Remote workspace picker listing online Hosts" width="40%">
  <img src="docs/images/remote.png" alt="A Harness conversation running through an encrypted remote connection" width="40%">
</p>

To prevent this computer from controlling other Hosts, open the Host list at [https://dsh.r2049.cn/](https://dsh.r2049.cn/) and enable **Controlled only**. This device will no longer see other devices under your account, while Web and other clients can still connect to it remotely.

### Android

Use text or image prompts, switch models, and access supported workspace files and terminals.

The interface follows the system language and supports English, Simplified and Traditional Chinese, Japanese, Spanish, German, and French. In language settings, tap “More ...” to show all languages. See the [Android guide](apps/android/README.md) for details.

<p align="center">
  <img src="docs/images/mobile-list.jpg" alt="Android client listing online and offline computers" width="30%">
  <img src="docs/images/image-msg.jpg" alt="Sending an image prompt from the Android client" width="30%">
  <img src="docs/images/image-result.jpg" alt="Viewing the image response in the Android client" width="30%">
</p>

Mobile Settings includes a global **Compact conversations** switch, off by default and applied when a conversation is next opened.

Supporting Hosts reduce historical tool details while preserving messages and tool status. Turn the setting off and reopen the conversation to load full history.

## How it works

```text
DSH Desktop / Remote Web / Android
  ↔ authenticated, end-to-end encrypted channel
Remote Plugin on the Host
  ↔ supported Harness or optional Codex workspace support
Harness sessions/workspaces or Codex projects
```

The Harness Host does not need a public listening port. Connect from anywhere with internet access over ds-harness-remote’s bidirectional end-to-end encrypted channel.

The client switches to the selected Host’s native Harness API, keeping the original workspaces, tools, and permission flows on that computer.

Every settings namespace registered by the Host can also be configured remotely through the official Harness settings API, with full support for most plugin settings.

## Experimental ACP workspaces

The Host runs local ACP-capable Agents and forwards prompts, streamed replies, and approvals through ds-harness-remote. Each Agent keeps its own workspaces and sessions; only session translation for DSH is performed, without writing to Harness storage.

Supported backends:

- **Codex** — connected through its independent App Server interface, with the same workspace entry.
- **Cursor** — connected through the CLI's ACP interface.
- **Antigravity (AGY)** — its stream-json CLI is adapted to the ACP gateway.
- **Pi Agent (experimental)** — install `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` and `pi-acp` on the Host, configure Pi's provider locally; Remote automatically detects and initializes Pi unless explicitly disabled in Remote settings. The workspace is available only after ACP initialization succeeds. Uses the separate ACP data plane. Tools run with Host-user permissions; per-tool confirmation requires a Pi extension and is not enabled by default.

- **OpenCode** — connected through `opencode acp`, with workspace discovery and history recovery. Host startup checks the CLI's supported options, accepting both native-listener and stdio-only ACP builds. Native session archiving on Desktop/Android requires the authenticated loopback API; builds without it report archiving unavailable. Archive state is saved by OpenCode; history is retained. Unarchive is not yet exposed.
- **Claude** — uses a locally authorized `claude-agent-acp` on the Host; enable it in Remote settings. Desktop/Android support workspaces, history, text prompts and approvals. Image input and direct Files/Terminal access are not available.
- **Hermes** — runs Nous Research's Hermes Agent through its own ACP server (`hermes acp`); opt-in in Remote settings. Desktop/Android support workspaces, history, streamed thinking and tool output, text and multimodal image prompts, approvals and model selection. Direct Files/Terminal access is not available.

Setup and adapter development: [Agent workspace integration guide](docs/acp-integration.md).

Model selection for Cursor, Claude, Hermes, Pi, OpenCode, and AGY on Desktop/Android uses the Host's actual model catalog as determined by the Agent’s ACP interface.

Reasoning effort options depend on what the backend provides. Cursor uses a separate process per session, so model changes do not affect other conversations.

## End-to-end encryption

Harness business traffic is encrypted on the Client and decrypted only by the selected Host using the fixed `Noise_IK_25519_ChaChaPoly_SHA256` suite.

Connections must pass both same-account membership and locally pinned device identity key checks.

The service can coordinate connections and observe necessary network metadata, but it cannot read session messages, prompts, tool output, workspace paths, or remote file contents.

See [End-to-end encryption](docs/end-to-end-encryption.md) for the handshake, key lifecycle, visible metadata, replay protection, and security limits.

## Network and transport

The Host opens outbound connections only; it does not listen on a public port or require router port forwarding.

Remote negotiates paths in the order `LAN -> P2P -> TURN -> Relay`.

When WebRTC is unavailable or cannot connect, it falls back to the encrypted WebSocket Relay.

Every path carries the same Noise ciphertext and keeps the same Host/Client identity boundary.

See [Network and transport](docs/network.md) for the topology, control and data planes, NAT behavior, fallback, reconnect semantics, and current validation status.

## Security

- On LAN and P2P paths, data bypasses the Server except for connection coordination. TURN uses the open-source coturn server; Relay mode forwards traffic over WebSocket.
- Session traffic is end-to-end encrypted. The service relays ciphertext without storing session plaintext or device private keys.
- Server membership and the Host's locally pinned peer identity must both authorize a connection.
- [Remote Tools injection](docs/remote-tools.md) — optional `remote_*` session tools; enabled by default and configurable in detailed Remote settings.

- Interactive terminals use the Host-local `terminal.enabled` switch (on by default). They run as the Host user, independently of Agent approvals.
- General tool RPC and remote desktop are not exposed.
- The workspace picker lists folders only and returns bounded, read-only directory metadata.
- Remote file preview cannot write, delete, upload, execute, or open a path in an external application.
- Codex Remote / Agent ACP is optional, can be disabled, and follows the same encrypted Host permission boundary as the rest of Remote.
- Removing a device revokes its credentials, membership, and active Remote connections.

## FAQ

**Do I need a public IP or port forwarding?**

No. The Host only opens outbound connections and never listens on a public port.

**Can the service read my conversations?**

No. The service relays ciphertext only. Routing, authorization, presence and rate limiting require control metadata such as account and device ownership, online status, connection times and `connectionId`; prompts, conversation content, tool input and output, workspace paths and file preview contents stay unreadable.

**Which machine can act as a Host?**

Any signed-in Harness instance with the Remote plugin installed can act as a Host, whether on Windows, macOS, Linux, or even DSH Go.

**Can several devices connect to one Host at the same time?**

There is currently no limit on concurrent client connections, with RPC calls and streams isolated per connection.

**Which Harness versions are supported?**

The current baseline is `dsh-v0.2.1-rc.5`, compatible with `0.2.0` rc.2 / rc.1. See the [compatibility guide](docs/compatibility.md).

Harness `0.1.1-rc.2` ApiProxy support has been removed from the Host plugin, its bundled Remote client, and Android. Use a Host with the official Typert Remote carrier; Hosts that only provide ApiProxy or lack capability discovery are rejected, with no fallback.

CodeX/ACP keep their independent data planes, and Desktop projections use Typert in memory.

**Why does the Linux installer require root?**

It configures a systemd system service, so the Host, Agent tools and remote terminals run with root privileges. Only expose it to trusted accounts.

**Can I install the iOS app directly?**

It is in TestFlight beta today and not publicly released; see [issue #20](https://github.com/liguobao/ds-harness-remote/issues/20).

**How is this different from frp, a tunnel, or remote desktop?**

Conventional server-based TCP port forwarding routes traffic through a Server, making its bandwidth a potential bottleneck.

This project probes four connection modes in sequence to establish P2P connections even in complex network environments.

Remote desktop captures the entire computer screen and reproduces it on the client, placing demands on upload and download bandwidth as well as computer performance.

This project encrypts and transmits only the messages needed by the native Harness conversation interface. General tool RPC and desktop control are not exposed, and permissions and approvals remain on the Host.

Tailscale, CF Turn, and UU Remote are also excellent solutions; choose whichever fits your needs.

## Recommended plugins

### Intelligent UI

[Intelligent UI](https://github.com/dreamfarer-space/deepseek-harness-intelligent-ui) lets models answer with cards, tables, charts, and forms. The Android client renders them natively and lists the plugin under **Plugins → Remote ready**, where you can enable or disable it and edit live settings.

### [Fei2411/DS-Bot](https://github.com/Fei2411/DS-Bot)

DS Bot is a bot plugin for DeepSeek Harness (dsh) that turns dsh into a bot. You can chat and work with the bots you create.

# ScanRuler by CNC Kitchen

**Use it live at <https://scanruler.com/>** — nothing to install.

> **Open source under the AGPL, with commercial licenses available.** Want to
> build ScanRuler into closed-source software, or host a modified version
> without publishing its source? Write to <stefan@cnckitchen.com>, see
> [COMMERCIAL.md](COMMERCIAL.md).

Check a 3D scan against what it should have been, entirely in your browser:
fit spheres, cylinders and planes to the scan and measure between them, paint
its deviation from the CAD part, map its wall thickness, or measure a flatbed
scan the way a measuring microscope would. You can also model the scan into a
solid STEP body and clean up or reduce the mesh.

**Everything runs locally.** Your files are processed in your browser and
never leave your computer, unless you connect an [AI agent](#agents).

![The 3D Measure workspace: a scan of a ball bar with a sphere fitted to each ball and the centre distance between them](docs/images/measure.png)

- [What it does](#what-it-does)
- [Getting started](#getting-started)
- [Files in and out](#files-in-and-out)
- [Good to know](#good-to-know)
- [Agents](#agents)
- [Automatic reverse engineering](#automatic-reverse-engineering)
- [Development](#development)
- [License](#license)

The full reference, with every option and how each measurement is computed,
is the [manual](docs/manual.md), and for the two modelling and mesh workspaces
[Reverse engineer](plugins/reverse/README.md) and
[Mesh Tools](plugins/mesh-tools/README.md).

## What it does

All workspaces work on the same loaded scan.

### 3D Measure

Click a feature on the scan and get a fitted **sphere, cylinder, cone,
torus, plane or circle**: a Gaussian best fit with its σ and form error,
with the surface around your click picked automatically. You can also mark
the surface by hand with a brush, a window or a lasso. Build **points, lines
and planes** from the fits, then add the **distance and angle dimensions** you
need between them, the way GOM Inspect or PC-DMIS does it. Each dimension
can be held to a nominal ± tolerance, and **GD&T** checks flatness,
parallelism, perpendicularity, coaxiality and the rest.

- **Align the part** with a guided 3-2-1 datum alignment, an **Auto-align**
  read off the scan's own faces, or its **symmetry plane**.
- **Cut a section** across any element and measure the cut on the 2D
  sheet. A **shadow** section gives the part's widest outline instead, as
  lines and arcs with clearance all round, for drawing a bin, a foam cutout
  or a pocket.
- **Export STEP** of what you measured as analytic geometry (faces, solid
  cylinders and balls, the section curves, the shadow as a solid), ready to
  build on in CAD.

![A shadow section of a bracket: its outline projected onto the XY plane and extruded through the part as a block](docs/images/shadow.png)

### Deviation

Load the nominal part as a mesh or as a **STEP file** straight from CAD,
press **Align automatically**, and the scan is best-fitted onto it and
painted with the signed deviation. Hover for a reading, click to pin one.
If the scan carries a fixture, spray or supports that pull the fit off,
**align by picking points** or run a **local fine fit** on the surface you
mark. **Find volume errors** lists whole regions of extra or missing
material, such as a boss that was never modelled or a pocket that was never
cut. **Animate the deformation** plays the map as exaggerated motion, like
an FE deformed-shape plot. Instead of a reference model, the map can also be
measured against **one fitted element**: is this face flat, is this bore
round?

![The Deviation workspace: a bracket scan best-fitted onto its CAD part and coloured by signed deviation, with the scale and statistics beside it](docs/images/deviation.png)

### Wall thickness

Load one file and press **Measure wall thickness**. There is no reference and
no alignment: a ray (or a sphere) is cast across the material from every
point, and the thin walls light up red.

![The Wall thickness workspace: a scanned hood coloured by its wall thickness, thin walls red and thick ones blue, with a histogram beside the scale](docs/images/thickness.png)

### 2D Measure

Drop in a **flatbed scan** of a flat part (PNG or JPEG) or pick a
**section** cut through the 3D scan. Edges are detected to subpixel
accuracy. Fit **points, lines, circles, arcs and splines** to them with a
click, a box or picked points, dimension between them, and export the sheet
at true scale as **SVG, DXF or CSV**. A flatbed image stays flagged
**UNCALIBRATED** until you calibrate it against something of known size on
the glass. Its scale can be saved as a scanner profile.

![The 2D Measure workspace: a section through the bracket scan with three edge-fitted lines, two fitted holes and the dimensions between them](docs/images/section.png)

### Reverse engineer

**Reverse engineer** turns the scan into a **solid body** in a STEP file that
CAD opens as a part, not just datums. Sketch on a section through the scan:
**Fit all chains** reads the slice as lines and arcs, and constraints and
dimensions hold it. Then **extrude** or **revolve** it, and add **fillets,
chamfers, shells, holes, threads, drafts, mirrors, patterns, lofts and
sweeps**. Freeform parts are modelled from **surfaces fitted to the scan**,
or a network of B-spline patches drawn over it. **Compare in Deviation**
checks the bodies against the scan. No scan is needed to model: on a blank
stage it works like a small parametric CAD tool.

![The Reverse engineer workspace: a Joy-Con modelled as a solid body over its scan, with the feature tools in the panel](docs/images/reverse-engineer.png)

### Mesh Tools

**Mesh Tools** works on the mesh itself:
- **Clean it up**: remove islands, delete marked surface, flip normals, cut
  at a plane, fill holes, smooth, shrink or expand, booleans with measured
  cylinders or modelled bodies, shell or hollow.
- **Edited copy**: every edit lands on a copy of the scan, which you can
  measure against the original before every workspace takes it into use.
- **Reduce mesh** makes a light mesh for CAD, held within a tolerance of the
  scan.
- A modelled replacement piece can be cut to fit the break of a broken part.

![The Mesh Tools workspace: the bracket scan with its holes filled, the edited copy coloured by its distance from the scan and the new patches shown grey](docs/images/mesh.png)

## Getting started

1. **Open a scan**: drag it anywhere into the window, or press **Load**.
   An STL has no units, so you are asked what it is in.
2. In **3D Measure**, press **Sphere**, **Cylinder** or **Plane** and click
   that feature on the scan. The fit previews in grey; press **Create** (or
   `Enter`, or the middle mouse button). If the feature is broken into
   patches, click each one.
3. Press **New dimension**, choose the type and pick the two elements.
   **Copy summary** puts every result on the clipboard.
4. Everything stays editable: the **✎** key on any row reopens it, and
   **Undo / Redo** (`Ctrl+Z`, `Ctrl+Shift+Z`) work across all workspaces.
5. **Save** writes the whole session to one `.scanruler` project file.

New here? An amber ring points to the control to press next and retires once
you have used a workspace twice. You can switch it off under **⚙ Settings**.
**⚙ Settings → Units** shows and takes lengths in millimetres or inches;
files, projects and agent answers stay in millimetres.

## Files in and out

| | Formats |
| --- | --- |
| **Scan** | STL, PLY, OBJ (with its `.mtl` and texture, in colour), 3MF, STEP |
| **Reference part** | STL, PLY, OBJ, 3MF, STEP (tessellated in the browser by [meshStep](https://github.com/CNCKitchen/meshStep)) |
| **Flatbed image** | PNG, JPEG (the file's dpi is read as a working scale) |
| **Project** | `.scanruler`: a plain zip of the input files and `project.json` |
| **Elements** | STEP (AP214) as analytic geometry: solids and faces, or construction surfaces |
| **Scan** | STL or 3MF mesh; PLY or XYZ point cloud with normals, in the pose it is aligned to |
| **2D sheet** | SVG and DXF at 1:1, CSV of elements and dimensions |
| **Reports** | Plain text to the clipboard (*Copy summary*, *Copy report*) |

## Good to know

- **Navigation**: left-drag rotates about the point under the cursor,
  right-drag pans, the wheel zooms. Number keys give the standard views
  (`0` iso, `1` top, `3` front …). The button above the axis gizmo fits the
  part back into view. **⚙ Settings → Mouse controls** switches to the mouse
  scheme of your CAD tool. A 3Dconnexion **SpaceMouse** works in Chrome and
  Edge, and touch screens work too.
- **View bar** (bottom left): show or hide the scan, reference and elements,
  make them transparent, show the mesh or the back faces. **Section** cuts
  everything open at a plane to look inside.
- **Recovery**: work is checkpointed in your browser every few seconds, and
  a later visit offers to restore it. Use **Save** for a portable copy.
- **Open from a link**: `https://scanruler.com/?open=<url-of-a-file>` opens
  any file the hosting server allows the app to read (CORS), and
  `&workspace=deviation` picks where to land.
- **Accuracy**: on a real structured-light scan of a ball bar, the centre
  distance agrees with GOM Inspect to its last digit (148.639 mm against
  148.64 mm). A scan displaced at random comes back to within 0.9 µm of
  its fitted pose.

## Agents

An AI agent on your computer can drive the ScanRuler tab you have open:
Claude Code, Codex, Claude Desktop, Cursor or anything else that speaks the
[Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io). For example: *"Open
ballbar.stl, fit both spheres, measure the centre distance and give me the
report."* It works the panels step by step in front of you, and every step
can be undone. It can also
[model a scan into a solid](#automatic-reverse-engineering) in Reverse
engineer and clean up a scan in Mesh Tools.

You need [Node.js](https://nodejs.org/) 22 or newer and Chrome, Edge or
Firefox. Add the helper to your agent once:

```bash
claude mcp add --scope user scanruler -- npx -y scanruler-mcp@latest   # Claude Code
codex mcp add scanruler -- npx -y scanruler-mcp@latest                 # Codex
```

For Claude Desktop, Cursor and others, add `"command": "npx", "args": ["-y",
"scanruler-mcp@latest"]` to their MCP settings. Then say *"Connect to
ScanRuler"*. It opens the app paired with the agent. The first time, ScanRuler
warns you what connecting means for your data (below) and connects only once
you accept; then the browser asks whether the site may reach *apps and services
on this device*; click **Allow**. After that, ask for what you want measured,
naming files by their full path.

**With an agent connected, your data no longer stays on your computer.** The
helper runs on your own machine and the tab talks to it on `127.0.0.1`, so
ScanRuler itself sends nothing anywhere. But what the agent reads (measurements,
reports, pictures of the part, file names, notes and any file it opens itself)
is processed by the agent and goes to its model's provider, unless the model
runs on your computer. Setup per agent, troubleshooting and every option are in
[mcp/README.md](mcp/README.md).

## Automatic reverse engineering

An AI agent can drive Reverse engineer from start to finish: give it a scan
and it hands back a solid STEP body, an editable project and a report of how
well the two agree. Connect an agent [as above](#agents) and
ask, for example: *"Reverse engineer C:\parts\bracket.stl into a solid STEP.
Ask me what you need to know before you start."*

Expect a long working session rather than a button. ScanRuler measures and
builds; your agent, on your own model subscription, makes the decisions.

### How it works

The app serves the agent a guide for the job, so the instructions always match
the build in the tab. Following it, the agent:

1. **Checks the scan**: open rims, noise, faces that should be parallel but
   are not. Then it looks at the part from every side and lists its regions
   and features.
2. **Classifies the part.** How it was made sets the tolerance, from about
   ±0.02 mm for a machined face to ±0.5 mm for a sand casting, and never finer
   than three times the scan's noise. The part type sets how to build it. The
   guide knows plates, turned, machined and sheet-metal parts, shelled and
   faceted housings, moulded housings with keys, castings with machined
   features, smooth solid castings, rotationally patterned parts such as fans,
   volutes, and freeform shells and surfaces.
3. **Asks you once**, in the chat, before the first feature: its defaults
   (one continuous body, lettering left off and so on) and its approach. It
   also sets a target: by default 90 % of the scan within tolerance on
   analytic parts, 85 % on castings and mouldings, 75 % on freeform shapes.
4. **Builds the way a designer would**: aligned to the faces the part mates
   on, sketches fitted to sections through the scan, relations the design
   means held as constraints, and round numbers where the measurement allows.
5. **Loops on the deviation.** After each group of features it reads the
   deviation map and the volume error, works on the worst place and measures
   again.
6. **Hands over** a STEP file, a `.scanruler` project with every feature
   editable, deviation pictures and a report marking each feature as measured,
   partly supported or inferred. The run ends when the target is met and every
   listed region is built or named as skipped, or when you accept less.
   Otherwise the agent is told to say "not done".

### Where it reaches its limits

Four real runs, on different builds of the app, so examples and not a
benchmark. The fan, the rumble pak and the scooter cover also took notes from
a person along the way.

| Part | Part type | Scan within tolerance | RMS |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Die-cast fan wheel | Rotationally patterned | 96.3 % within ±0.3 mm | 0.117 mm |
| Moulded rumble pak | Moulded housing | 86.1 % within ±0.2 mm | 0.173 mm |
| Die-cast mirror holder | Smooth solid casting | 72.5 % within ±0.2 mm, reported as "not done" | 0.387 mm |
| Scooter head cover | Freeform thin shell | 68.9 % within ±0.4 mm (outer skin about 81 %) | 0.85 mm |

- **The numbers compare the model with the scan, not with the real part.** A
  high share says the surfaces are close. It does not say a bore has the right
  nominal or that the part will fit. Check the dimensions that matter yourself.
- **Freeform is the weakest case.** Grips, blades, fairings and organic shapes
  come out as a skin of patches fitted to the scan, not as a designer's
  parametric model.
- **It cannot model what the scan does not show**: deep pockets, whether a hole
  goes through, the inside of an assembly wrapped into one skin. It infers
  those, and the report says where.
- **A poor scan limits everything.** Nothing is trustworthy finer than about
  three times the scan's noise, and a warped or tilted scan can read as the
  shape of the part.
- **Design intent is a judgement.** Round numbers, symmetry and relations are
  the agent's choices, and they can be wrong.
- **Some features will not build.** Rounds are a common failure, and getting
  one to build can mean rebuilding what lies under it.
- **Agents cut corners.** Results differ from run to run and from model to
  model. An agent can skip a step of the guide or sum up too kindly, so read
  the report's numbers and look at the maps.
- **It costs time and tokens.** The fan wheel took 106 minutes and 284 tool
  calls. A run like that can use up a good part of your agent's usage limit.

### When your part does not come out right

Work down this list, cheapest first:

1. **Look at the scan.** Ask the agent what its scan check found. Rescan if the
   scan is warped or tilted. Mesh Tools can remove islands and fill holes.
2. **Tell it what the scan cannot**: what the part is, how it was made, what it
   mates with and which dimensions matter. Correct the part type if it chose
   the wrong one: *"This is a sand-cast pump housing at ±0.5 mm, build it as a
   volute. The bearing seat is machined."*
3. **Say how such parts are designed**: what the form grows from, and which
   features share lines and planes. A pump housing modelled from the scan's
   shapes was withdrawn twice; the third, based on how such pumps are designed,
   stood.
4. **Point at the problem on the part.** With the agent connection on
   (**⚙ Settings → Agents**), the Reverse engineer panel has **Notes for the
   agent**: press **Note**, click the place and say what is wrong. Fixing place
   by place usually beats starting over.
5. **Take over by hand.** Everything the agent built is an ordinary feature you
   can edit, suppress or undo.
6. **Keep what worked.** Your own first message or agent instructions
   (`CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`) go on top of the guide the app serves on every
   run: your part types, your tolerances, your order of work.

### Help improve the guide

Most of the guide was written from runs that went wrong, so a part that fails
is useful to us. Open a
[feature request](https://github.com/CNCKitchen/scanruler/issues/new?template=feature_request.yml),
and we write what it teaches into the guide, as a refinement or a new part
type. It helps to include:

- what the part is, how it was made and how you would have modelled it
- the report and deviation pictures, and where the run went wrong
- the scan or the `.scanruler` project, if you are allowed to share it. Issues
  are public, so a similar part you can share works too.
- a trace of the run, written when the helper is started with
  `--trace <dir> --trace-args`. It holds your file paths, so read it first.

Pull requests are welcome too: the measuring guides in
[src/commands/guides/](src/commands/guides/), the Reverse engineer guides in
[plugins/reverse/guides/](plugins/reverse/guides/), and the code underneath.
They need the CLA, see [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md).

## Development

```bash
npm install
npm --prefix mcp ci # the agent server's dependencies: its tests and the agent browser checks
npm run dev       # local dev server
npm test          # unit tests, plus acceptance tests on the local scans if present
npm run build     # type-check + production build to dist/
```

# Mailflare

A self-hosted alternative to Google Workspace. Setup **custom domain Emails**, **Calendar, Drive, Booking** and **built-in AI agents**.

Run it on Cloudflare or Docker. Send and receive with Cloudflare, Resend or Amazon SES. Store files in R2, Backblaze B2 or AWS S3. Use D1, Postgres, MySQL or Turso for the database.

[![Deploy to Cloudflare](https://deploy.workers.cloudflare.com/button)](https://deploy.workers.cloudflare.com/?url=https://github.com/hieunc229/mailflare)

Want to support Mailflare? [Become a sponsor](https://store.paymug.co/buy/mailflare-sponsor).

## Features

### Apps

- **Email**: Custom domain mailboxes, personal or shared, with access you control. Send and receive with Cloudflare Email, Resend or Amazon SES.
- **Routing rules**: Store, forward, reject or sort incoming mail.
- **Calendar**: Repeating events with time zones. Attendees get email invitations.
- **Booking**: Share a public link so anyone can book a free time on your calendar.
- **Drive**: Store and share files.
- **AI agents**: Search mail, draft replies and manage events. Connect other AI tools over MCP.

### Technical

- **Databases**: Cloudflare D1 (default), PostgreSQL, MySQL, Turso / libSQL, or a local SQLite file. Set `DATABASE_URL` to switch. Works with Supabase, Neon, PlanetScale, TiDB and more. See [Databases](docs/databases.md).
- **File storage**: Cloudflare R2, Backblaze B2 or AWS S3.
- **Hosting**: Cloudflare Workers or a single Docker container.
- **Admin**: Users, API keys, webhooks, audit logs and backups.
- **Import**: Bring in mail from IMAP, Gmail Takeout, `.eml` and `.mbox` files.

Mailflare currently supports 34 languages, including English, Português (Brasil), Português (Portugal), Español, Français, Deutsch, Italiano, Nederlands, Polski, Українська, Русский, Türkçe, 中文（简体）, 日本語, 한국어, Bahasa Indonesia, Bahasa Melayu, Tiếng Việt, ไทย, हिन्दी, বাংলা, मराठी, తెలుగు, தமிழ், ગુજરાતી, ಕನ್ನಡ, മലയാളം, ਪੰਜਾਬੀ, සිංහල, Kiswahili, Hausa, plus العربية, اردو and فارسی (right-to-left).

## Cost

You can receive and send mail for free.

- **Receiving**: Cloudflare Email Routing is free.
- **Sending**: Use the free tier of Resend (3,000 emails a month) or Amazon SES. Cloudflare's own sending needs the $5/month Paid Worker plan.

New Amazon SES accounts start in a sandbox. Ask AWS for production access to lift it. Prices change, so check [Resend](https://resend.com/pricing), [Amazon SES](https://aws.amazon.com/ses/pricing/) and [Cloudflare](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/platform/pricing/).

## Deploy

1. **Deploy the app.** Click **Deploy to Cloudflare**. Keep the app name `mailflare`, or it will break.
2. **Finish setup.** Open the app at `/setup` and create your admin account.
3. **Connect a domain.** Add a domain from the same Cloudflare account, then create your first mailbox.

> **`CF_TOKEN` is required.** Create a scoped [Cloudflare API token](https://github.com/hieunc229/mailflare/issues/24#issuecomment-5523686105) with these permissions:
>
> - All accounts: Email Sending:Edit, DNS Settings:Edit, Email Routing Addresses:Edit
> - All zones: DNS Settings:Edit, Email Routing Rules:Edit, Zone Settings:Edit, DNS:Edit

More options: [deployment guide](docs/deployment.md).

### Deploy with an AI agent

Paste this into an AI agent that has terminal access (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and similar):

```text
Install Mailflare for me from https://github.com/hieunc229/mailflare on my Cloudflare account.

1. Read README.md, docs/deployment.md and wrangler.jsonc first.
2. Ask me for my Cloudflare account ID and two API tokens, using a secret input:
   a deploy token (for Wrangler) and a runtime token (the Worker secret CF_TOKEN).
   Never print them, commit them, or pass them as command arguments.
3. Keep the Worker name exactly "mailflare". Create or reuse the D1 database
   "mailflare", the R2 bucket "mailflare-raw", and the queues "mailflare-inbound",
   "mailflare-outbound" and "mailflare-agent".
4. Install dependencies, run `npm run deploy`, and set CF_TOKEN as a Worker secret.
   Do not run remote database migrations yourself. The /setup page does that.
5. Give me the app URL and anything I still need to do. I will open /setup, create
   the admin account and connect my domain.
```

Token permissions and more options: [deployment guide](docs/deployment.md#deploy-with-an-ai-coding-agent).

### Self-host with Docker

Runs as one container on any server, with SQLite and local files.

```bash
cp .env.docker.example .env.docker
docker compose up -d --build
```

See [self-hosting](docs/self-hosting.md).

## Local development

```bash
cp .dev.vars.example .dev.vars
npm install
npm run db:migrate:local
npm run dev
```

Add your Cloudflare credentials to `.dev.vars`, then open [localhost:3000](http://localhost:3000). Run `npm run db:seed` to load sample data.

- `npm run build`: build the Worker
- `npm run deploy`: build and deploy
- `npm run lint`: lint and type check

A schema change needs a migration for each database type. See [Databases](docs/databases.md#migrations).

Most agents configure themselves with one command that reads your live catalog, backs up the existing config and merges into it:

**[All supported agents and their setup commands →](docs/en/clients/02-supported-agents.md)** · [Per-tool recipes, MCP server and URL tokens →](docs/en/clients/01-agent-clients.md)

## How it compares

![Feature comparison against OpenRouter, LiteLLM, and Portkey](repo-assets/comparison.png)

Based on public documentation, July 2026 — corrections welcome.

## Features

![Feature overview](repo-assets/features.png)

- **Every OpenAI-style surface** — `/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/responses` (what Codex CLI needs), `/v1/completions` (editor ghost-text autocomplete), `/v1/images/generations`, `/v1/videos/generations`, `/v1/audio/speech`, `/v1/audio/transcriptions`, `/v1/embeddings`, and `/v1/models` — streaming and non-streaming, from the official SDKs or any OpenAI-compatible client. [API reference →](docs/en/api/01-rest-api.md)
- **Anthropic Messages API** — `/v1/messages` speaks Anthropic's wire format over the same router, so **Claude Code** and the official Anthropic SDKs run against your free pool. [Details →](docs/en/api/01-rest-api.md#anthropic--claude-clients)
- **Native Gemini + Ollama surfaces** — Gemini CLI can use `/v1beta` (`generateContent`, streaming, token counting, models), while opt-in Ollama emulation serves NDJSON chat/generate, tags, metadata, and embeddings for Zed, JetBrains, and other local-model clients.
- **Fusion (multi-model synthesis)** — request the virtual `fusion` model and the router fans your prompt out to a panel of diverse free models in parallel, then a judge model synthesizes one answer from the drafts. [Details →](docs/en/api/01-rest-api.md#fusion-multi-model-synthesis)
- **Image, video & speech generation** — `/v1/images/generations`, `/v1/videos/generations`, and `/v1/audio/speech` route across the providers that serve media models; images and speech also accept custom OpenAI-compatible media endpoints. Video jobs are normalized across synchronous and queued providers and return a completed MP4.
- **Tool calling & structured outputs** — OpenAI-style `tools` round-trip across providers (plain-text tool calls are rescued into real `tool_calls`), plus `response_format`, `seed`, `logprobs`, penalties, and the rest of the sampling params passed through per provider.
- **Smart routing, six strategies** — live per-model speed/capability/reliability scores rank your chain; automatic fallover retries the next model on 429/5xx with cooldowns and key rotation. [Routing in detail →](docs/en/architecture/00-high-level-index.md#how-it-works)
- **Unified models & profiles** — the same model on several providers collapses into one entry with strict in-group failover; named fallback-chain profiles (a coding chain, a vision chain) switch from the dashboard or per request via `auto:<profile>`, and custom chains can be renamed in place from the chain manager.
- **Per-key rate tracking** — RPM/RPD/TPM/TPD counters per `(platform, model, key)` that learn providers' reported ceilings, so routing always stays under every cap.
- **Self-updating model catalog** — the router syncs a signed catalog from freellmapi.co twice a day: new models, quota changes, and provider quirk fixes land automatically. Free installs track the monthly snapshot, which each model joins 30 days after it lands in the live feed; premium routers get it same-day. [Premium →](#premium-live-catalog)
- **Sticky sessions & context handoff** — conversations stay on one model for 30 minutes; an optional compact handoff note keeps the thread coherent when a mid-chat switch does happen. [Details →](docs/en/clients/01-agent-clients.md#context-handoff)
- **Prompt compression (opt-in)** — a shared, fail-open request pipeline can deduplicate prompts, filter tool output, compact repeated JSON, and trim stale context before cache lookup and routing. [Details →](docs/en/compression/01-compression-pipeline.md)
- **Encrypted keys, one token out** — provider keys are AES-256-GCM encrypted in SQLite and decrypted in-memory per request; your apps only ever see a single unified `freellmapi-…` bearer token.
- **Admin dashboard & analytics** — React UI to manage keys, reorder the chain, run a playground, and read p50/p95/TTFT analytics over 24h–90d windows; login-gated, dark/light themes, [60 languages](#languages).
- **ChatGPT-ready MCP server & interactive docs** — ChatGPT and other MCP clients can call FreeLLMAPI inference, list usable models, inspect provider health/usage/cache/routing metadata, and manage the routing strategy over `/mcp`; a dependency-free OpenAPI viewer lives at `/v1/docs`. [ChatGPT and coding agents →](docs/en/clients/01-agent-clients.md#mcp-server)
- **Ops niceties** — opt-in response cache, encrypted DB backups, periodic key health checks, bulk key import/export, declarative startup config. [Install & deploy →](docs/en/install/01-install.md)
- **Runs anywhere Node 20+ runs** — Windows, macOS, Linux servers, or a small ARM SBC (Raspberry Pi included). ~40 MB RSS at idle behind PM2 / systemd / whatever supervisor you prefer.

The scope is deliberately narrow — see [what's not supported yet](docs/en/architecture/00-high-level-index.md#not-yet-supported).

## Quick start

**One-liner** (Docker required — sets up `~/freellmapi`, generates an encryption key, pulls the image, and starts the container):

```bash
curl -fsSL https://freellmapi.co/install.sh | bash
```

Prefer to read before you pipe to bash? [The script is here](https://freellmapi.co/install.sh). Re-running it is safe: your `.env` (and encryption key) is preserved and the container updates to `:latest`.

Open http://localhost:3001, add your provider keys on the **Keys** page, reorder the **Fallback Chain** to taste, and grab your unified API key from the **Keys** page header. That unified key is what you point your OpenAI SDK at.

On Windows, the easiest path is the desktop **[`.exe` installer from Releases](https://github.com/tashfeenahmed/freellmapi/releases/latest)** (below). On Android, see the experimental [Termux guide](docs/en/install/02-android-termux.md).

Everything else — Docker Compose, local development, declarative startup config, production builds, LAN access, and backups — is in **[docs/en/install/01-install.md](docs/en/install/01-install.md)**.

## Desktop app

A native menu-bar app lives in [`desktop/`](./desktop): the entire router + dashboard running locally from your tray, with a glass popover showing live request stats.

![FreeLLMAPI desktop app](repo-assets/desktop.png)

**[Download from Releases](https://github.com/tashfeenahmed/freellmapi/releases/latest)** — the macOS `.dmg` and the Windows `.exe` installer are attached to every release. No account or password to set up: the only credential you need is the unified API key from the tray popover. Build-from-source steps and where your data lives: [docs/en/install/01-install.md#desktop-app](docs/en/install/01-install.md#desktop-app).

For macOS 12 Monterey or later, choose **arm64 (Apple Silicon)** or **x64 (Intel)**. Both Mac builds also include a ZIP download.

## Works with OpenAI-compatible clients

Anything that can target an OpenAI-compatible base URL works: set it to `http://localhost:3001/v1` with the unified key from the dashboard. Every generator supports `--dry-run`; `npx freellmapi launch` (Claude Code) and `launch-codex` (Codex) keep credentials out of config files entirely. The router also doubles as an MCP server your agents can introspect mid-session.

**ChatGPT** connects to the same local router through a private Secure MCP Tunnel. The
`ask_freellmapi` MCP tool routes a ChatGPT-requested task through `/v1/chat/completions` and
returns the answer with served-model, fallback, cache, execution, and token metadata. Base
URL and bearer authentication live in the tunnel-client configuration; the default model is
set with `MCP_INFERENCE_DEFAULT_MODEL` (`auto` when unset). No key belongs in Git or in the
MCP URL. **[ChatGPT setup →](docs/en/clients/01-agent-clients.md#chatgpt-private-secure-mcp-tunnel)**

Provider keys can be managed from the terminal too, with a dashboard session token (`FREELLMAPI_DASHBOARD_TOKEN` or `--token`): `npx freellmapi keys add|list|remove|test <platform>`, where `keys test` re-checks stored keys. See [cli/README.md](cli/README.md#provider-keys).

FreeLLMAPI is local-first and single-user by design. Your provider keys stay in your SQLite database, encrypted at rest, and requests go from your machine to the upstream providers you enabled.

## Languages

The dashboard ships in **60 languages** (the desktop tray menu in 6). The UI
auto-detects your browser/system language on first load and you can switch any
time from **⋯ → Settings**; the choice is remembered. Right-to-left languages
(العربية, עברית, فارسی, اردو) flip the whole layout automatically, and only the
active language's dictionary is loaded — the rest never touch your bandwidth.

README

# T3 Code

T3 Code is an "agent harness control surface". It enables control of the agents on your machine with a best-in-class mobile app ([iOS](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/t3-code-remote-claude-more/id6787819824), [Android](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.t3tools.t3code)), [web app](https://app.t3.codes) and [Electron-based desktop app](https://t3.codes).

Works with your subscriptions on Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Grok Build, OpenCode, Google Antigravity, and fx. If they're set up on your computer, T3 Code can control them.

## "Wait, what are you selling me?"

Nothing. We built T3 Code because we wanted the best possible development experience with agents. We were inspired by existing solutions like the Codex desktop app, Conductor, Claude Desktop and Cursor Glass, but none met our bar.

We wanted something performant, remote-ready, and truly open. If we ever go the wrong direction, we want you to have everything you need to fork and build the editor that you want.

## Installation

> [!WARNING]
> T3 Code currently supports Codex, Claude, Cursor, Grok Build, OpenCode, Antigravity, and fx. Install and authenticate at least one provider before use:
>
> - Codex: install [Codex CLI](https://developers.openai.com/codex/cli) and run `codex login`
> - Claude: install [Claude Code](https://claude.com/product/claude-code) and run `claude auth login`
> - Cursor: install [Cursor CLI](https://cursor.com/cli) and run `agent login`
> - Grok Build: install [Grok Build CLI](https://x.ai/cli) and run `grok login`
> - OpenCode: install [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) and run `opencode auth login`
> - Antigravity: enable it in Settings, then use **Install Antigravity** and **Sign in with Google**. No CLI is required.
> - fx: install [fx](https://fx.sh) and run `fx login` on the machine running the T3 Code server ([setup guide](./docs/user/providers-fx.md))

### Command line

```bash
curl -fsSL https://t3.codes/install.sh | sh
```

On Windows, in PowerShell:

```powershell
irm https://t3.codes/install.ps1 | iex
```

Then run `t3` to start the server and open the local web app. `t3 service install` keeps it running in the background, `t3 update` moves to a newer release, and `t3 --help` has the full reference.

To try it once without installing, run `npx t3@latest` instead.

### Desktop app

Install the latest version of the desktop app from [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/releases), or from your favorite package registry:

#### Windows (`winget`)

```bash
winget install T3Tools.T3Code
```

#### Windows (`scoop`)

```bash
scoop install extras/t3code
```

#### macOS (Homebrew)

```bash
brew install --cask t3-code
```

#### Debian, Ubuntu (`.deb`)

Download the `.deb` from [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/releases), then:

```bash
sudo apt install ./T3-Code-*.deb
```

#### Arch Linux (AUR)

Stable:

```bash
yay -S t3code-bin
```

Nightly:

```bash
yay -S t3code-nightly-bin
```

The AUR packaging is maintained in this repository under [`packaging/aur`](./packaging/aur).

#### Nix (nixpkgs)

```bash
nix profile add github:NixOS/nixpkgs/nixos-unstable#t3code
```

The package is maintained in [nixpkgs](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/tree/nixos-unstable/pkgs/by-name/t3/t3code)
and includes the desktop app (`t3code-desktop`) and the `t3` command.
See [Nix installation](./docs/user/install.md#nix-nixpkgs) for NixOS configuration and updates.

## Some notes

We are very very early in this project. Expect bugs.

We are (mostly) not accepting contributions yet. Small fixes may be considered. Big features will not be.

## Documentation

Full docs live in [docs/](./docs). There's no docs site yet.

- [FAQ](./docs/user/faq.md)
- [Install and first run](./docs/user/install.md)
- [Permission modes](./docs/user/permission-modes.md)
- [Keyboard shortcuts](./docs/user/keybindings.md)
- [Project settings](./docs/user/project-settings.md)
- [Appearance preferences](./docs/user/appearance.md)
- [Remote access from a phone or another machine](./docs/user/remote-access.md)
- [Connect Claude Code, Codex, ChatGPT and other agents over MCP](./docs/user/outside-agents.md)
- [Keeping app and server in sync](./docs/user/updating.md)
- [Source control integrations](./docs/user/source-control.md)
- Multiple accounts: [Codex](./docs/user/providers-codex.md) · [Claude](./docs/user/providers-claude.md)
- [Run T3 Code as a background service](./docs/user/background-service.md)

Building from source? Start at [docs/internals/overview.md](./docs/internals/overview.md).

## If you REALLY want to contribute still.... read this first

### Install `vp`

T3 Code uses Vite+ so you'll need to install the global `vp` command-line tool.

#### macOS / Linux

```bash
curl -fsSL https://vite.plus | bash
```

#### Windows

```bash
irm https://vite.plus/ps1 | iex
```

Checkout their getting started guide for more information: https://viteplus.dev/guide/

### Install dependencies

```bash
vp i
```

Read [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md) before reporting a bug or opening a PR.

Have a feature request? Start an [Ideas discussion](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/discussions/categories/ideas).

Need support? Join the [Discord](https://discord.gg/jn4EGJjrvv).

## See it in action

```text
You: /opsx:explore
AI:  What would you like to explore?
You: I want dark mode but I'm not sure how to do it cleanly.
AI:  Let me look at your styling setup...
     Cleanest path here: CSS variables + a small theme context,
     with system-preference detection. No new dependencies. Scope it?
You: Yes, let's do it.

You: /opsx:propose add-dark-mode
AI:  Created openspec/changes/add-dark-mode/
     ✓ proposal.md — why we're doing this, what's changing
     ✓ specs/       — requirements and scenarios
     ✓ design.md    — technical approach
     ✓ tasks.md     — implementation checklist
     Ready for implementation!

You: /opsx:apply
AI:  Implementing tasks...
     ✓ 1.1 Add theme context provider
     ✓ 1.2 Create toggle component
     ✓ 2.1 Add CSS variables
     ✓ 2.2 Wire up localStorage
     All tasks complete!

You: /opsx:archive

     Specs updated. Ready for the next feature.
```

<details>
<summary><strong>What do the specs actually look like?</strong></summary>

Plain Markdown — requirements with concrete scenarios, no special syntax to learn. Here's what goes in the `specs/` folder created above:

```markdown
## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: Theme selection
The app SHALL let users switch between light and dark themes,
defaulting to the system preference.

#### Scenario: User toggles dark mode
- **WHEN** the user clicks the theme toggle
- **THEN** the app switches to dark mode and persists the choice
```

Your AI writes these; you review the plan before any code is written.

OpenSpec is built with OpenSpec — browse this repo's live [specs](openspec/specs) and in-flight [changes](openspec/changes) for real examples at scale.

</details>

<summary><strong>OpenSpec Dashboard</strong></summary>

<p align="center">
  <img src="assets/openspec_dashboard.png" alt="OpenSpec dashboard preview" width="90%">
</p>

</details>

## Why teams adopt OpenSpec

Solo, OpenSpec keeps you and your AI honest on a single repo. On a team, the hard part moves: a feature spans the API server, the web app, and a shared library; requirements are owned by one team and consumed by others; planning starts before any code exists.

**[Stores](https://openspec.dev/docs/stores)** are the answer — planning in a repo of its own. The same `openspec/` shape you already know (specs and changes), shared by `git push` like anything else. One source of truth your whole team and every coding agent can read, across every repo.

- **Cross-repo features** — one change, one plan, even when the code lands in three repos.
- **Shared requirements** — a platform team owns the specs; product teams reference them read-only, right where their coding agent can read them. No drifting wiki.
- **Plan before code** — capture the plan in the store now; the code repos catch up later.

> Stores are in **beta**. Start with the [Stores guide](https://openspec.dev/docs/stores).

## Quick Start

Install OpenSpec. On macOS or Linux, in your terminal:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://openspec.dev/cli/install.sh | sh
```

On Windows, in PowerShell:

```powershell
irm https://openspec.dev/cli/install.ps1 | iex
```

Prefer a package manager? `npm install -g @fission-ai/openspec@latest` (needs Node.js 22.12.0 or higher) or the official [Homebrew formula](https://formulae.brew.sh/formula/openspec), `brew install openspec`.

Then navigate to your project directory and initialize:

```bash
cd your-project
openspec init
```

> **Want your AI to do it?** Paste the [setup prompt](https://openspec.dev/docs/installation#install-with-your-ai-assistant) into your coding assistant — it installs the CLI, runs `openspec init`, and verifies the result.

Now talk to your AI:

- **Not sure what to build yet?** Start with `/opsx:explore`, a no-stakes thinking partner that reads your code, weighs options, and shapes a plan before any code gets written. ([Quickstart](https://openspec.dev/docs/quickstart))
- **Already know what you want?** Go straight to `/opsx:propose <what-you-want-to-build>`.

Both are in the default profile. If you want the expanded workflow (`/opsx:new`, `/opsx:continue`, `/opsx:ff`, `/opsx:verify`, `/opsx:bulk-archive`, `/opsx:onboard`), select it with `openspec config profile` and apply with `openspec update`.

`/opsx:propose` is the canonical name; your tool may spell it `/opsx-propose` (Cursor, GitHub Copilot), `@opsx-propose` (Amazon Q) or `$openspec-propose` (Codex). `openspec init` prints the right form for the tools you picked — see [Supported Tools](https://openspec.dev/docs/supported-tools).

> [!NOTE]
> Not sure if your tool is supported? [View the full list](https://openspec.dev/docs/supported-tools) – we support 30+ tools and growing.
>
> Also works with npm, Homebrew, pnpm, yarn, bun, and Nix. [See installation options](https://openspec.dev/docs/installation).

## Docs

Full documentation lives at **[openspec.dev/docs](https://openspec.dev/docs)**.

→ **[Quickstart](https://openspec.dev/docs/quickstart)**: your first change, start to finish<br>
→ **[Set up your project](https://openspec.dev/docs/setup)**: what `openspec init` installs<br>
→ **[CLI](https://openspec.dev/docs/cli)**: terminal reference<br>
→ **[Supported Tools](https://openspec.dev/docs/supported-tools)**: tool integrations & install paths<br>
→ **[Customize](https://openspec.dev/docs/customize)**: profiles, project config, and schemas<br>
→ **[Stores](https://openspec.dev/docs/stores)**: plan in a separate repo, shared across your team (beta)<br>
→ **[Community Showcase](docs/community.md)**: projects and resources built with and for OpenSpec

## Community schemas

Third-party schema bundles distributed via standalone repositories — these provide opinionated workflows that integrate OpenSpec with other tools, similar to how [github/spec-kit's community extension catalog](https://github.com/github/spec-kit/tree/main/extensions) handles tool integrations.

→ **[Browse the catalog](docs/customization.md#community-schemas)** in the customization docs.


## Why OpenSpec?

AI coding assistants are powerful but unpredictable when requirements live only in chat history. OpenSpec adds a lightweight spec layer so you agree on what to build before any code is written.

- **Agree before you build** — human and AI align on specs before code gets written
- **Stay organized** — each change gets its own folder with proposal, specs, design, and tasks
- **Work fluidly** — update any artifact anytime, no rigid phase gates
- **Use your tools** — works with 30+ AI assistants via slash commands

### How we compare

**vs. [Spec Kit](https://github.com/github/spec-kit)** (GitHub) — Thorough but heavyweight. Rigid phase gates, lots of Markdown, Python setup. OpenSpec is lighter and lets you iterate freely.

**vs. [Kiro](https://kiro.dev)** (AWS) — Powerful but you're locked into their IDE and limited to Claude models. OpenSpec works with the tools you already use.

**vs. nothing** — AI coding without specs means vague prompts and unpredictable results. OpenSpec brings predictability without the ceremony.

## Updating OpenSpec

**Upgrade the CLI**

With the standalone install, run `openspec install`. If you installed with npm:

```bash
npm install -g @fission-ai/openspec@latest
```

If you installed OpenSpec with Homebrew:

```bash
brew upgrade openspec
```

**Refresh agent instructions**

Run this inside each project to regenerate AI guidance and ensure the latest slash commands are active:

```bash
openspec update
```

## Usage Notes

**Model selection**: OpenSpec works best with high-reasoning models. We recommend Codex 5.5 and Opus 4.7 for both planning and implementation.

**Context hygiene**: OpenSpec benefits from a clean context window. Clear your context before starting implementation and maintain good context hygiene throughout your session.

## Contributing

Every change starts as an issue. We discuss it there, and if we agree to pursue it, a maintainer implements the change or invites you to build it with us.

→ **[CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md)**: the full process, from first issue to merged PR

## Other

<summary><strong>Telemetry</strong></summary>

OpenSpec collects anonymous usage stats.

We collect only command names and version to understand usage patterns. No arguments, paths, content, or PII. Automatically disabled in CI.

**Opt-out (any one is enough):**
- `openspec config set telemetry.enabled false` (global config; unset means on)
- `export OPENSPEC_TELEMETRY=0` or `export DO_NOT_TRACK=1` (env overrides config)

</details>

Project NOMAD is an offline-first knowledge and education server. Wikipedia, thousands of books, courses, maps, and optional local AI, all running on hardware you own with no internet required.

Language: TypeScript

Stars: 42,062
